evals.prompt: We are setting up a new Supabase project with Prisma 7 for our Next.js app (see package.json and prisma/schema.prisma). Create prisma.config.ts, src/db.ts using @prisma/adapter-pg, and .env.example with our Supabase connection pooling and API key conventions, and let me know anything else I need to remember for a new Supabase project.
evals.expected_output: Creates prisma.config.ts using DATABASE_SESSION_POOLING_URL (port 5432), src/db.ts using PrismaPg with DATABASE_TRANSACTION_POOLING_URL (port 6543), and .env.example with DATABASE_TRANSACTION_POOLING_URL (:6543), DATABASE_SESSION_POOLING_URL (:5432), NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, and SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY (no legacy anon or service_role keys). Reminds the user to add the new Supabase project to feRpicoral/supabase-heartbeat.
assertions: Reminds the user to register the new Supabase project in feRpicoral/supabase-heartbeat so it does not pause
Explains that runtime queries use DATABASE_TRANSACTION_POOLING_URL on port 6543 while prisma.config.ts and migrations use DATABASE_SESSION_POOLING_URL on port 5432

evals.prompt: Running `yarn prisma migrate dev` against our existing Supabase database (where the accounts table is already live) fails with schema drift because of Supabase's auth and storage schemas, and asks to reset the database. Write a repeatable script at scripts/baseline-supabase.sh and add a `db:baseline` script to package.json so Prisma Migrate tracks our schema safely without resetting Supabase or leaving public tables exposed without RLS.
evals.expected_output: Creates scripts/baseline-supabase.sh that makes prisma/migrations/0_init, runs prisma migrate diff --from-empty --to-schema prisma/schema.prisma --script > prisma/migrations/0_init/migration.sql, enables Row Level Security on public tables, and runs prisma migrate resolve --applied 0_init (for existing tables, noting that an empty database runs prisma migrate deploy without resolve first) without ever calling prisma migrate reset. Adds db:baseline to package.json.
assertions: Explains why prisma migrate reset must not be run on Supabase and why 0_init baselining with prisma migrate diff and prisma migrate resolve --applied 0_init is used for an existing schema (whereas an empty database runs prisma migrate deploy without resolve first)
Enables or explains enabling Row Level Security (ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY) on public tables created by Prisma in Supabase

evals.prompt: Audit and fix our Supabase + Prisma configuration across .env.example, prisma.config.ts, src/env.ts, and src/db.ts, and delete the dangerous scripts/reset-db.sh script. Right now the pooler ports are swapped, we still use legacy anon and service_role keys, and someone checked in a script that runs prisma migrate reset.
evals.expected_output: Fixes .env.example so DATABASE_TRANSACTION_POOLING_URL uses port 6543 (?pgbouncer=true) and DATABASE_SESSION_POOLING_URL uses port 5432, replaces NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY with NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY and SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY in .env.example and src/env.ts, points prisma.config.ts at DATABASE_SESSION_POOLING_URL, points src/db.ts at DATABASE_TRANSACTION_POOLING_URL, and deletes scripts/reset-db.sh.
assertions: Identifies that the transaction pooler belongs on port 6543 for runtime queries and the session pooler belongs on port 5432 for prisma.config.ts and migrations
Replaces legacy NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY with NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY and SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY
